description: Renovate owns dependency updates for this repository because Dependabot cannot.
GitHub lists Bun as supported for version updates but NOT for security updates, so the
config-free security-update path falls back to the npm_and_yarn updater, which cannot read
bun.lock and fails with dependency_file_not_supported. No .github/dependabot.yml fixes that;
there is no ecosystem entry that unlocks Dependabot security updates for Bun. Renovate has a
dedicated bun manager instead, which reads the text bun.lock and the packages/* workspaces.
Operator coupling worth knowing before changing repository settings: Dependabot ALERTS and the
dependency graph must stay ENABLED even though Dependabot SECURITY UPDATES are turned off.
Renovate's vulnerabilityAlerts reads GitHub's alert feed; disabling alerts blinds it.
baseBranchPatterns is a product-history guard, not a style preference. Archon was rewritten
(#957) and the Python-era product was archived rather than deleted. It still lives on
archive/v1-stable and archive/v1-task-management-rag, which between them carry
python/pyproject.toml, python/uv.lock, archon-ui-main/package.json, docs/package.json, several
python/Dockerfile.* and their own docker-compose.yml - manifests of a product that no longer
exists. Naming the working branch is what keeps Renovate off them. Leaving this key out would
make correctness depend on the repository's default-branch setting, which breaks silently if
someone flips the default to main (releases go through main, and AGENTS.md forbids committing
to it directly, so Renovate PRs must never target it) or adds a base branch later. A plain
string matches exactly - only the /regex/ form consults the branch list - so 'dev' cannot
widen to archive/*. The current option name is baseBranchPatterns; the older baseBranches has
been removed from the schema.
Off by Renovate default, and the reason this file exists. Most of this repository's exposure
is not a declared range that is too old - it is a range that already permits a patched
version while the frozen bun.lock resolves to a stale one. That class produces no GitHub
alert at all, because the range *could* resolve to something patched, so no amount of
alert-driven automation finds it. Regenerating the lockfile does, and deleting bun.lock then
running bun install is exactly what Renovate's bun manager does here.
This is also why the outcome does not lean on vulnerabilityAlerts: that path defaults to
rangeStrategy 'update-lockfile', and Renovate's docs omit bun from the managers supporting
that strategy, so alert-driven PRs may no-op. The scheduled regeneration will not.
